evidence.quote:
Description: The amount of time an agent is actively working on a work item in their console. Active time is tracked only for tasks routed using the tab-based capacity model. It’s tracked only when the work tab is open and in focus in the console. If the agent switches console tabs, the time spent on the other tabs isn’t counted. Active time continues to count if you switch to a new browser tab or window.
Active time stops when the agent closes the work item or the after conversation work time ends, whichever happens first.

Add Multiple Objects When the Stream Represents a Domain

One benefit of a custom channel is grouping multiple compatible event entities. A CustomerUpdates__chn channel could contain Account and Contact CDC members, allowing the consumer to subscribe to one domain-oriented channel rather than managing independent subscriptions.

That does not mean every integration should create giant channels. Keep the channel aligned to a coherent consumer contract.

leadDispositions.lead: Temporal completeness of alert qualification, including conditions that become true without a write
leadDispositions.reason: The completed-policy candidate already distinguishes CDC data changes from clock-only conditions and proposes centralized timer/refresh policy. General event/CDC foundations remain prior skips P2/P3, and broader notification foundations remain B-N1. No new parent concept is established.

leadDispositions.lead: Operational notification lifecycle and feedback-system foundations
leadDispositions.reason: B-N1 already records the broad low-utility parent. The new suppression concept already retains the concrete Email-to-Case feedback mechanism. Do not inflate it into a second broad parent concept.

leadDispositions.lead: Native Flow scheduled-path admission, batching and retry semantics for time-based Case alerts
leadDispositions.reason: S3 covers general asynchronous outbound delivery; B-N4 covers activation and B-N3 covers repeat scheduling. The cited primary snapshot additionally describes scheduler-specific admission deferral and retry/rollback behavior. Those mechanics are not stated by the inspected canonical claims for the 19+4 coverage. Their relevance depends on choosing native scheduled Flow as an actual alternative. This is a source lead, not a new accepted claim or scored concept.

leadDispositions.lead: Migration of queued native scheduled paths when a new Flow version removes or renames a path
leadDispositions.reason: The existing rule-versioning concept explicitly owns this question. It may justify a narrow external follow-up, but a new concept title alone would double-count B-N4. TASK-2030 specifies the custom worker and does not settle native platform migration behavior.

leadDispositions.lead: Filter-safe episode rearming: preserve disqualifying and closure transitions when selecting a CDC stream
leadDispositions.reason: The proposed application contract explicitly requires all relevant qualifier exits, closure and deletion transitions. It forbids qualifier-only upstream filters by default, requires qualified coverage if narrowing, and says current-state repair cannot reconstruct unseen historical episodes. No provider filter-selection guarantee is invented.

leadDispositions.lead: Unsupported calculated or derived Case values and source refresh
leadDispositions.reason: The new polling concept explicitly covers the non-persisted-value limitation and scheduled/event-triggered reads. The actual Case field list is a D1/deployment qualification, not another public-source research concept. Do not infer Case-specific field behavior from UserPresence/AgentWork examples.

leadDispositions.lead: Date-driven reminders can recur when the time-source field moves
leadDispositions.reason: The new suppression concept explicitly records recurring field-based scheduling and eligibility cancellation. TASK-2030 owns custom durable timer and episode choices. No additional default cooldown, interval or once-ever policy follows from the source.

leadDispositions.lead: Replayed enrichment must not override bound historical qualification
leadDispositions.reason: The baseline already documents that unchanged replay enrichment can reflect current database values. The new contract owns immutable revision binding. Applying both constraints is a consistency check, not a new independent concept.

leadDispositions.lead: Cross-Case Email-to-Case notification amplification and interruption
leadDispositions.reason: B-N3 now explicitly retains cross-Case creation feedback and an implementation-specific send switch. R3-N1 covers a different, previously skipped CDC write-back/changeOrigin loop; do not merge those mechanisms. A recipient-loop classification or cross-record correlation design could extend B-N3 only if an email sink into Email-to-Case is actually selected. The present project sends no such demonstrated sink traffic.

leadDispositions.lead: Actual channel/principal/org identity and metadata visibility
leadDispositions.reason: The completed Omni candidate supplies a documented read-only procedure. Whether the intended principal can query and subscribe remains D2/D3 and target-org execution. A public source cannot resolve local credentials, entitlements or actual Case visibility.

leadDispositions.lead: CDC channel filter revision and replay selection semantics
leadDispositions.reason: Tooling metadata and replay enrichment are documented separately. The inspected canonical outputs do not state whether changing a channel-member predicate changes which retained events are selectable during replay, or what selection revision applies. This is external channel-configuration behavior, distinct from TASK-2030 application-rule binding. It is not yet evidence of a defect or a complete concept.

leadDispositions.lead: Flow runtime API upgrades versus logic-version activation
leadDispositions.reason: B-N4 already explicitly distinguishes the inherited runtime API version from a new rule/Flow logic version. Do not count the release boundary again as frontier novelty.

leadDispositions.lead: Topic capability checks versus delivery and predicate acceptance
leadDispositions.reason: R1-N1 already distinguishes GetTopic metadata/capability from event-delivery and filter correctness. C10 owns representative/failure tests. Actual delivery needs separately authorized target execution; source-only metadata cannot establish it.
